column5: How do you make Bash scripts safe?

```bash
PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
```

```bash
[[ -z "${1:-}" ]] && { echo "Usage: $0 <arg>"; exit 1; }
```

**Logging**:
```bash
exec > >(tee -a "$logfile") 2>&1
```

**Parameter expansion safety**:
```bash
rm -rf "${dir:?dir not set}"/*
```

column6: • Assess the Failure: Determine the nature of the storage failure (logical, physical, or both). • Isolate the Device: Isolate the failed storage device to prevent further damage or data loss. • Verify Backups: Confirm the availability and integrity of recent backups. • Use Data Recovery Tools: Explore data recovery tools that may be able to recover data from the failed storage device. • Engage Data Recovery Services: If necessary, consider engaging professional data recovery services for physical damage or complex issues.
